note: Interest on Australian Government Securities. Budget Paper No. 1 expects it to rise each year to 2029-30 as debt servicing costs grow.

Interest that accrues on the unfunded superannuation owed to current and former Australian Government employees, including the military. It is an accounting expense, calculated at a 5.0% discount rate from 2026-27.
Untied payments to state, territory and local governments, which they spend as they choose. Payments tied to a purpose, such as hospitals or schools, are counted under that function instead.
Payments to the states under the Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements, mostly for disasters that have already happened. No provision is made for future disasters, so the estimate falls each year.

Amounts not yet assigned to an entity: an allowance for estimates being revised up, decisions taken but not yet announced, items kept confidential for commercial or national security reasons, and an offset for expected underspends.
The states' share of GST revenue plus the Australian Government's top-up to the GST pool.
The "No Worse Off" guarantee: top-ups so that no state receives less GST than it would have under the previous distribution system. Extended to 2029-30.
ACT municipal services and royalty payments.
Untied grants to local councils, paid through the states. $2.9 billion of the 2026-27 funding was paid early, in 2025-26.
Mostly Australian Government funding to the states and territories for veterans' hospital services.
